newsitem.title: JAPAN: FTC tells NTT to cut stake in cellular unit--paper.
newsitem.headline: FTC tells NTT to cut stake in cellular unit--paper.

text.p: Japan's Fair Trade Commission (FTC) has told Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) to drastically cut its stake in its cellular phone unit, the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Friday.
No officials from the FTC or NTT were immediately available for comment.
The FTC, Japan's antimonopoly watchdog, told NTT to cut its stake in the cellular unit, NTT Mobile Communications Network Inc, or NTT DoCoMo, to about 10 percent, the paper said.
NTT DoCoMo is currently 95-percent owned by NTT, the paper said.
Nihon Keizai quoted the FTC as saying it would use legal action if necessary to force NTT to reduce its DoCoMo stake.
The FTC also urged NTT and DoCoMo to cut their respective stakes in the NTT group's personal handy phone system (PHS) operator, NTT Chuo Personal Communications Network Inc, the paper said.
NTT currently has a 28 percent stake and NTT DoCoMo has a 48 percent stake in the PHS unit.
